collection.intro: Depending on the features you use, we may process the information below. Information for disabled features is generally not collected:
collection.item1: Account and registration data: username, display name, avatar, email address or mobile number and verification status, password hash, account state, roles, and permissions. We do not store a directly recoverable plaintext password.
collection.item2: Sign-in and security data: sign-in time, IP address, browser or device data, session and token status, captcha result, abnormal behavior, and risk-control records.
collection.item3: API and key information: verification hashes, encrypted key ciphertext, prefixes, suffixes, status, permissions and IP allowlists. The current program supports permission-controlled key decryption and viewing; it does not store only irreversible hashes. Calls may also record APIs, methods, necessary parameters or redacted summaries, status, latency, traffic, upstream identifiers, billing results and call identifiers.
collection.item4: Order and asset data: purchased package or points, order number, amount, payment channel and state, channel transaction identifier, refund, and reconciliation records. Payment credentials are generally processed directly by the payment provider.
collection.item5: Submitted and displayed information: friend-link applications, contacts, feedback, tickets, attachments, supporter names and messages. Contact details needed for review and replies should not all become public merely upon application. Explain the scope and lawful grounds before submission or display.
collection.item6: Device and local-storage data: cookies and local data used for sign-in assistance, language, theme, remembered username, and other interface preferences.
collection.warning: Submit only necessary information you are entitled to process. Do not put passwords, complete keys, payment credentials or unrelated sensitive details in URLs, parameters, attachments or messages. Redaction cannot identify and remove every possible input. Check legal conditions before sensitive, minor-related or cross-border processing.
collection.title: 3. Information We Process
collection.item7: Content, caching and risk information: links, bodies or files needed by the API, potentially cached responses, request fingerprints and redacted risk samples according to configuration. URLs, filenames and responses may themselves contain personal information. Explain actual fields, cache duration and recipients rather than promising that every request and response is never persisted.

cookies.item1: The platform may use HttpOnly refresh-session cookies and browser local or session storage for necessary access state, language, theme and remembered usernames. HttpOnly limits direct script reading of that cookie; it does not mean there are no other stored tokens or session-exposure risks.
cookies.item2: You can clear or restrict cookies and local storage in the browser, but persistent sign-in, personalization, or security functions may stop working correctly.
cookies.item3: Verification, payment, advertising and content providers may load scripts that access network, device or interaction information. Unnecessary analytics or advertising tracking must not be enabled by default without appropriate lawful grounds. Disclose actual providers and purposes instead of labeling everything essential to login.
cookies.title: 5. Cookies, Tokens, and Local Storage

minors.item1: Services primarily target developers and organizations with suitable legal capacity. Use and payments by minors must fit their age, understanding and legal capacity and involve guardian guidance. This policy cannot replace valid guardian consent.
minors.item2: Processing personal information of children under fourteen requires guardian consent, dedicated rules and other applicable protections. An instance without the necessary arrangements should not actively offer processing directed at that group. Investigate inappropriate collection promptly, restrict processing and delete or take other lawful necessary measures.

purpose.intro: Each activity requires a specific lawful basis and must be necessary and relevant to the stated purpose. Improving service, security or accepting terms is not unlimited permission:
purpose.item1: create and manage accounts and provide sign-in, identity checks, password recovery, notices, and support;
purpose.item2: create and manage API keys, forward API requests, return results, and display call records;
purpose.item3: calculate calls, points, or fees and process orders, payments, refunds, reconciliation, and asset changes;
purpose.item4: prevent account theft, abuse, scraping, attacks, fraud, duplicate billing, and other security risks;
purpose.item5: Necessary troubleshooting and service-quality analysis, using aggregated or effectively anonymized data where possible. Re-identification, profiling, marketing, training or additional uses require a separate lawful-basis assessment and the corresponding notice and other obligations.
purpose.item6: comply with law and regulation, resolve complaints and disputes, and protect users, the operator, and third parties.
purpose.title: 4. Why We Use Information

retention.item1: Use the shortest period necessary for a defined purpose. Accounts, orders, security audits, caches, tickets and backups need separate periods or determination criteria. Legally required or unresolved-dispute retention is limited to necessary records, scope and duration, not indefinite preservation.
retention.item2: Delete or effectively anonymize when purposes are fulfilled or periods expire. Where deletion is not yet legally due or technically feasible, restrict processing as required to necessary storage and protection. Backups need controlled access and rotation; restores must respect completed deletion requests rather than revive unrestricted use.
retention.item3: Locations depend on deployment, hosting, upstream and third-party settings; this policy does not presume all information stays domestically. Before overseas provision, satisfy applicable notice, separate-consent, assessment, certification, standard-contract or other requirements, or establish an applicable exemption. An API call alone does not establish compliance.
retention.title: 8. Storage and Retention
retention.item4: “Hide”, “clear” or age-based automatic hiding of call logs changes user-side visibility only. It does not mean database records or backups have been deleted. Submit a personal-information deletion request through the rights channel; the operator must distinguish UI actions from actual retention and explain lawful grounds and periods or criteria.

rights.intro: Subject to applicable law, you may request to:
rights.item1: access, copy, correct, or supplement account and personal information;
rights.item2: delete information that is no longer necessary, was processed unlawfully, or must be deleted by law;
rights.item3: close the account, withdraw consent-based authorization, or restrict or object to certain processing;
rights.item4: receive explanations about automated decisions or third-party sharing and exercise other statutory rights.
rights.outro: Use available profile controls for supported changes; contact the operator for manual access, copying, deletion, account closure, withdrawal or other requests not supported in the interface. Verify only necessary identity information, preferably through verified accounts or email, without routinely requesting unrelated documents. Respond within statutory deadlines and explain progress, refusal grounds and appeal channels. Internal feedback is not a prerequisite to statutory complaints or court action.
rights.title: 11. Your Information Rights
rights.item5: Request explanations of processing rules, refuse significant decisions made solely through automated decision-making, and request human review where legally applicable. A risk-control hit does not itself establish illegality.
rights.item6: Withdrawal does not invalidate prior processing lawfully based on consent. Account closure does not automatically extinguish unsettled transactions or mandatory retention. Withdrawal from unnecessary processing must not block unrelated basic service.

security.item1: The current program offers password hashing, encrypted keys with permission controls, encrypted settings, some log redaction and risk controls. The operator must correctly configure HTTPS, access, key custody, patches, backups and audit. Available capabilities do not establish certification, absolute security or encryption of every field in this instance.

Notices should explain known impact, measures and contacts. Do not conceal confirmed material risks or treat a cyberattack as automatic immunity.
security.item3: Protect your account, password, and API keys. Never place a key in a public repository, frontend source, or untrusted client. Disable or rotate leaked credentials immediately and contact the operator.

legalBasis.title: 2. Lawful grounds and separate choices
legalBasis.item1: Identify the applicable lawful grounds for each activity: necessity for a contract to which you are a party, statutory duties, valid consent or another statutory basis. “Operational needs”, “better experience” or acceptance of service terms is not a basis for unrestricted processing.
legalBasis.item2: Consent-based processing requires informed, voluntary, explicit consent and a withdrawal channel. Meet separate-consent requirements for sensitive information, independent recipients, public disclosure and cross-border transfers where applicable. Do not bundle unnecessary processing into basic service access.
legalBasis.item3: Sensitive information needs a specific purpose, sufficient necessity and strict protection, explanations of necessity and impact and legally required assessments. Do not accept such inputs without the conditions being met. User submission does not automatically excuse the operator.

logs.title: 9. Call logs, caches and troubleshooting
logs.item1: Necessary billing review, troubleshooting and security may record times, IPs, API and call identifiers, status, latency, charges and request summaries. Call content and risk samples may contain personal information. Limit fields and staff access; a “technical log” label does not remove privacy protection.
logs.item2: Remove credentials and unnecessary content before logging where possible, covering query strings, callbacks, stack traces, ticket attachments, CDN and proxy logs. Automated masking cannot guarantee recognition of all custom fields, encodings or files. Do not copy complete production data into public support channels.
logs.item3: Configured response caches, Redis, files and databases may each retain copies. Clearing one list, cache or account does not prove deletion everywhere. Check associated copies, entrusted providers and recovery workflows, and explain scope and lawful exceptions to requesters.
